body.p: , after , , , , . Replaces the rest of 's "streamable="yes" runs unstreamed": xsl:source-document streams the bodies it can, and the stylesheet option of 19.10 is in xslt.h. Accepts 7.6a's Proposed item (the option), not its streamed principal source (below).

item.p: The parser (src/xml.c, xml_internal.h): an incremental parse (glossary ) is the same parse whose content walk stops after a visit whose events asked to pause and goes on when resumed; validation is refused. The concrete syntax tree is still made for the whole document first ().

The evaluator (src/evaluator_stream.c, part "stream"): a new IR kind STREAM, one step (child or descendant, node test, at most one predicate, numeric or boolean as in 4.4.1) from a node, its body in the selected node's focus, a counter slot for the position in a whole path, OPENS_DOCUMENT for the document of xsl:source-document. A stream builder keeps the open elements with their namespaces and attributes and queues the events; content nobody reads is skipped, a body that consumes its node gets a full stream window (its subtree, captured as the events pass), a body that reads its node only through stream points of its own gets a shallow window and the node becomes the open node (glossary , ). Windows go through fn:doc's document preparation (whitespace stripping). A STREAM whose origin is not an open node walks the tree, so a document the resolver gives as a node, a node of a full window and an unstreamed node take the same IR. The parser never calls the evaluator: STREAM tasks resume it (). The loader opens a streamed document as fn:doc resolves it (sxml_processor_document_loader_open_streamed) and does not keep it.

Lowering (src/xslt_lower_stream.c): a body is streamed when its instructions (through literal result elements whose attributes are motionless) are motionless and grounded by 7.6a's analysis (new sxml_xslt_assess_sweep) except at most one stream point (glossary ): an xsl:for-each without xsl:sort or separator whose select is a downward path of child steps, "//" or descendant:: as the last step, each with at most one motionless predicate, and whose body is at most consuming. Bodies reading fn:has-children, fn:path, fn:last, fn:function-lookup, xsl:call-template or attribute sets are not shallow (a window lacks siblings; a streamed selection has no size).

Not streamed yet (lowered unstreamed as before, same results by 19.10): accumulators (any declared), validation and type on xsl:source-document, xsl:apply-templates and streamable modes, xsl:iterate, xsl:fork, xsl:merge, aggregates over a streamed path (count(//x)), attribute steps at the end of a path, the principal source (a host gives it as a tree; a streamed principal source would be an additive xslt.h field). In XT40, 164 executions of xsl:source-document stream.

Option (xslt.h, additive last field, 's rule for stable headers): falls_back_to_unstreamed; the XSLT driver claims the feature streaming-fallback and sets it for the cases that depend on it. supports-streaming is true.

Measured: the allocator peak of streaming a generated document with a for-each over its records is 232 KB at 2.4 MB, 8.3 MB and 106 MB (tests/evaluator_stream_test.c runs 2.4 MB under a 1 MB limit, which the unstreamed run exceeds). The process's resident memory for 106 MB was 3.98 GB, almost all tree-sitter's syntax tree of the whole input (): a 1 GB document is out of reach until content is tokenized incrementally (the gate's "1 GB under 64 MB" holds for the allocator, not the process). XT40 (release, whole suite) 11,797 to 11,804 passed, none lost: streaming-fallback-001 to -006, system-property-012; merge-097sf is now run and fails on uri-collection with ?select=.
